newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jet Services plan bigger aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Jet Services plan bigger aircraft.

text.p: French road and air express distribution company, Jet Services, said it planned to introduce a bigger aircraft on its nightly all-cargo route between Kassel in Germany and its hub at Paris/Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport operated by subsidiary company, Axor.

"The service, which was launched last month, has proved such a success and there's a strong chance by the end of the year we'll have switched from a 2.5 tonne-capacity Metroliner we currently use to a six-tonne Fokker 27," a Jet Services official told Reuters.
The Kassel-CDG route forms part of Axor's European "next-day" express service which currently covers France, the Benelux, Germany and the U.K..
Also last month, Axor launched a Coventry-CDG freighter route with a 1.5 tonne-capacity Short SD300 aircraft.

"The Coventry-CDG service has made a satisfactory start and as with the Kassel service, if the volume of traffic warranted extra capacity, we would be ready to introduce a Metroliner-type aircraft, for example," the official said.
Axor also operates a nightly freighter route between Liege and CDG.
Later this month, Axor is to extend its network to Switzerland, Italy and Spain but in an inital phase, at least, traffic to and from these countries will be transported by road, the official added.
"However, air cargo services remain a longer term option if there was a steady growth in the volume of shipments."

Apart from Metroliner and SD300 aircraft, Jet Services, via its airline subsidiary, Air Jet, also operates a fleet of three BAe 146 QC (quick change) aircraft. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
